reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's rendered text (the fiend story told to Honey-Host inside The Three-Breasted Princess) and re-read and approved the corrected text.
Blockers fixed before approval: the frame teller was corrected, and the omission of the fiend's threat to eat the traveller is now disclosed in the adaptation changes.
The fiend is comic and vain, and the traveller escapes by keeping his wits; no em dashes; content note truthful.
illustrations: Six equal 512px panels; seams measured exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024 on the published WebP; 1024x1536, under 650 KB; no gutters, dividing lines, bleed or vignettes; no text in any panel.

Final sheet is a composite: panels 4 and 6 are from the original generation and panels 1, 2, 3 and 5 from one edit pass that matured the traveller's face to an adult of about twenty-five; colour matches across the seams.

The traveller (white dhoti and shirt, cotton cross-body bag, walking stick) is consistent; the thick bag strap does not read as a sacred thread. The fiend (green, round-bellied, orange hair, small horns, red loincloth, wooden-bead necklace) is comic, with no fangs, claws or weapons, and never grabs or hits.

Panel 2 shows the fiend's soft clean feet hanging in front of the traveller's chest. Panel 4: the fiend leaps into a lotus lake. Panel 5: the traveller runs off while the fiend dunks. Panel 6: the fiend waves and shouts from waist-deep water as the traveller walks far away toward the village.

The bead necklace was judged a plain wooden-bead necklace, consistent with the fiend keeping a vow, and not mocking any community. Accepted minor issues: small blunt cartoon teeth in panels 4 and 6, the traveller's face is tiny in panel 5, and a North-Indian style temple tower sits in the far background of panel 6.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age suitability has not been tested with children.
Source fidelity was checked against the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels; not every scene was checked in the app in dark mode.
